title: code-review-pr-scratchpad-avery-kim
content:
Quick scratchpad for PR #482 (kv-cache refactor) — notes while reviewing.

High-level summary:
- PR aims to centralize KV cache lifecycle and introduce per-model shards to reduce lock contention.
- Touches: runtime/cache/*, runtime/serving/session_manager.rs, tests/cache_integration.rs
- Perf claim: ~20% p99 latency improvement under mixed traffic (bench results in PR description).

Primary review checklist (do a pass for each):
- Correctness
  - [ ] Ensure no regression in KV cache correctness (eviction, ttl semantics, snapshot/restore).
  - [ ] Confirm durability assumptions: are we relying on in-memory only or writing metadata to disk? PR says in-memory with optional persistence flag.
  - [ ] Check handling of concurrent reads/writes: session_manager now holds a ShardMap; look for ABA/race windows (esp. session teardown).

- API/Surface area
  - [ ] Public APIs unchanged? Search for breaking pub(crate)/pub changes.
  - [ ] Config flags documented (shard_count, persistence_mode). docstring updates present?

- Performance & benchmarks
  - [ ] Verify bench harness: is the traffic shape realistic (token lengths, batch sizes)? Bench script at tools/bench/kv_bench.py — sample workload uses batch=8, seq=2048, which matches infra baseline.
  - [ ] Confirm CI doesn't flip on microbench-only assertions. Remove any flaky perf assertions.

- Tests
  - [ ] Unit tests updated for new sharding logic (see tests/cache_unit.rs) — some TODOs left in code ("// TODO: verify cross-shard eviction ordering"). Follow up required.
  - [ ] Integration tests: cache_integration.rs added but currently marked ignore on CI (#[ignore]) — needs justification.

- Safety & SRE concerns
  - [ ] Memory growth: shard map increases overhead. Are we tracking rss/heap in SLO dashboards? Add a metric for shard_count in telemetry.
  - [ ] Migration path: rolling restart safe? If older nodes still run non-sharded cache, will they talk to new nodes? Need a compatibility note.

- Docs/Runbook
  - [ ] Add runbook blurb for eviction storms and mitigation (reduce shard_count, lower ttl).
  - [ ] Release notes: mention config flags and default behaviour change (if any).

Refactor ideas / smaller suggestions (inline comments already added):
- Move ShardMetrics out of shard impl into a shared metrics collector to reduce duplication.
- Consider using dashmap instead of Mutex<HashMap> per shard for less explicit locking — but be mindful of iteration cost.
- session_manager.rs: split lifecycle management and lookup helpers into separate modules. Right now file is ~600 LOC, hard to grok.
- Introduce a thin trait for CacheBackend so we can swap in-memory vs persisted easily (helps tests).

Follow-ups (create tickets / assign):
- RUNTIME-450: Add e2e test for mixed-version cluster (non-sharded <> sharded). Priority: high. Owner: Jordan.
- RUNTIME-451: Add telemetry metrics for shard_count, per-shard-avg-entries, and eviction-rate. Owner: Avery.
- RUNTIME-452: Convert ignored integration test to CI-friendly by reducing flakiness (owner: Priya).

Minor nits / style
- Prefer descriptive commit messages for refactors (explain invariant changes).
- Use matches! macro in a couple of pattern checks (see session_manager.rs lines ~310-320).
- Small docstring typos fixed inline.

Repro steps (local):
- Checkout PR branch: git fetch && git checkout pr/482-kv-sharding
- Run unit tests: cargo test --workspace --tests --release
- Run bench: python3 tools/bench/kv_bench.py --batch 8 --seq 2048 --duration 60
- Run docker integration: ./scripts/local-integration.sh --focus cache_integration

Open questions / unresolved:
- Why was persistence removed from default? PR mentions "rarely used" but we have customers who rely on warm-start. Need a short convo with product.
- Is shard_count auto-configured? If so, what's the heuristic? I couldn't find it in config defaults.

Decision log (ideas for reviewer to consider):
- If backward compatibility is non-trivial, gate sharding behind an opt-in flag for first release.
- Prefer smaller incremental refactors vs big rewrite in one PR — less risk.

Action items for me:
- [ ] Follow up with author (Jordan) on ignored integration test justification and persistence rationale.
- [ ] Draft RUNTIME-451 telemetry ticket and add example Grafana panel template.
- [ ] Re-run bench with different seq distributions (256/1024/2048) and attach graphs to PR.

Random notes / scratches:
- observed a tight loop in session_manager that re-acquires lock during eviction — might explain p99 improvements when sharded.
- possible memory leak when shard entries hold Arc references to contexts; add weak refs?
- total LOC changed: ~+400; large PR. Consider splitting if possible.

Notes to self: keep review small and focused on correctness first (eviction + concurrency), then perf, then docs/telemetry.

-- Avery
